text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL

- Telefonica International Romania and Zephir Consortium -- led by telecom groups Motorola Inc of the U.S. and Tele Danmark of Denmark -- have contested results in a tender for Romania's two lucrative GSM licences awarded to MobilRom and MobilFon consortia.
- Romania needs $2.0 million daily to finance imports for its winter energy needs.
ADEVARUL
- The leu exchange rate dropped from 5,000 lei for a dollar to about 4,000 lei in exchange shops in the past week.
- Romania got an EBRD $85.9 million loan for road rehabilitation.

- The Central Bank (BNR) and National Securities Commission should be more active in promoting Romania's capital markets, John Heywood, executive president of Price Waterhouse Central and Eastern Europe said in interview.
- Romanian oil refineries are close to running out of crude due to lack of finace to pay for imports.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Korea's Daewoo Securities Co Ltd and Koram Bank to set up Daewoo Bank Romania with a 75 billion lei capital.
- BNR pledged to impose financial austerity with the help of Romania's new government.
- Three refineries in Ploiesti, Onesti and Navodari expected to be temporarily closed due to crude shortage.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's foreign debt is worth $7.0 billion, while hard currency reserves are worth a total of 2.1 billion, 800 million of which are held by the BNR.
- Company arrears reached 20,000 billion lei this year, or 21 percent of gross domestic product.
- Monthly inflation reached 3.4 percent in October.
- Energy leaks can waste up to 40 percent of the country's energy production.
- No bidder registered so far for Romania's 15 oil blocks on tender until November 30.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- Inflation at the end of 1996 could reach 45 percent, BNR governor Mugur Isarescu said.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Adrian Nastase, executive president of the Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), defeated in elections, insists moving the lower Chamber of Deputies into the palace built by dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.
- The newspaper publishes reactions by politicians on the designation of Victor Ciorbea, present mayor of Bucharest, as Prime Minister.

- The mayor of the western city of Timisoara, cradle of the December 1989 revolution, invited President-elect Emil Constantinescu and designated Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea to attend the ceremonies marking seven years since the outbreak of the revolution on December 16.
ADEVARUL

- Appointing Adrian Severin, vice-president of former Prime Minister Petre Roman's Democratic Party, as Foreign Minister would damage the credibility of the new cabinet. It recalled his support for the a recommendation of the Council of Europe's parliamentary assembly on ethnic minorities and suggests this would cause difficulties with Romania's Hungarian minority.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) could get the portfolio of Minorities Ministry, to be created instead of the present Council for Minorities.
ZIUA

- Some 113 billion lei ($32 million) were spent so far to appropriate the rooms for the lower Chamber of Deputies in Ceausescu's palace. Nastase said the upper house, the Senate, should also move into the huge building, which would cost another 10 billion lei ($2.8 million).
LIBERTATEA
- The newspaper publishes a list of possible ministers.
- The reorganisation of the state television according to a law adopted in 1994, but not applied so far, is one of the issues to be solved quickly by the new parliament, says the newspaper.
CRONICA ROMANA
- One of the top priorities will be to ensure energy supplies for the winter, says designated Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea in an interview.
- Incumbent Ion Iliescu lost the presidential run-off because his leftist PDSR was incapable of concluding broad alliances, said Iosif Boda, Iliescu's campaign manager.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- The National peasant Party (PNT-CD) will get 10 to 12 ministries, the Liberals four and Roman's Social Democrats six, said sources close to the commission of negociators to build the new government. ($=3,509 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
